headline: Highest risk is capability conflict: Gemini CLI can write/modify the same filesystem and git state that the course repo may occupy, while prompt-injection and leakage are limited by the course agent’s lack of runtime surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a non-runnable course repo with no io_surfaces, while agent B can read files and use MCP. A direct injection path is not documented, but if A’s content is manually copied into B or placed in a shared workspace, B could misread it as instructions. The pathway is unusual and the blast radius is small.
conditions: IF agent_a content is manually copied into agent_b prompts or files
IF agent_b is pointed at a shared directory containing attacker-controlled text
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate directories
Do not paste repo text into B prompts
Disable MCP servers not needed for the task
Use a read-only copy of A for review
Add a short provenance note before any copied text

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches no data classes and has no runtime I/O, so it cannot leak operational data. Agent B can read local files and send context to external APIs, but the pair does not show a shared sensitive workspace or PHI/PII handling. Leakage is therefore limited to ordinary repo contents if the operator places them in B’s cwd.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in agent_b.cwd
IF agent_b is given credentials or secrets in its shell environment
mitigations: Keep secrets out of B’s working directory
Use a throwaway clone for B
Unset unnecessary environment variables before launch
Review MCP server access before enabling it
Store sensitive inputs outside the shared repo

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent B has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and broad network egress, with shared state explicitly via filesystem and git. Agent A is a repo artifact, so if both are used around the same checkout, B can overwrite or race with the course materials. The default overlap is dangerous because git/file changes can be irreversible or hard to unwind.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout
IF agent_b is allowed to commit or rewrite files in A's repository
mitigations: Use separate clones per agent
Run B in a disposable branch
Pause B before any git commit
Enable filesystem snapshots or backups
Restrict B to read-only access for A's repo

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a course repository and B is an action-capable coding agent. If A’s materials are fed into B as guidance, B may treat them as authoritative without a verification step. The pair does not prove automated downstream actions, but B can execute shell and modify git, so mistaken instructions can cascade into incorrect code or commits.
conditions: IF A's text is used as an instruction source for B
IF B is permitted to act on generated code without human review
mitigations: Require human review before commits
Ask B to cite the exact source line it used
Separate reference docs from executable workspaces
Add a verification checklist before shell actions
Limit B to draft-only mode for first pass

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data handling mismatch is evidenced. Agent A is an open-source course repo with no touched data classes, and agent B’s documented surfaces only show local files, shell, and optional Google API use. Without a specific regulated data flow, a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into agent_b's workspace
IF a deployment policy requires residency or retention guarantees not shown here
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Confirm workspace data classification before use
Disable external API calls for sensitive tasks
Document retention settings for B
Use a separate compliant environment if regulated data is required
